finding.expected: Resolve the canonical remote task lifecycle as mandatory evidence before materialization. Require its main_sha to equal the authorized main SHA and require exactly one valid RESULT operational tip whose RUN id and candidate SHA equal the authorized cumulative tip. Propagate remote query, decoding, ambiguity, missing-tip, and mismatch failures as CorrectionIntegrationError before commit-tree/update-ref. Do not fall back to local branch identity as canonical authority. Add focused regressions for remote-main-ahead, remote lifecycle unavailable/malformed, missing tip, and competing tips; each must create no integration ref/candidate.
finding.issue: integrate_correction does not fail closed while proving the exact canonical authorization binding. It prefers the local refs/heads/main value over canonical remote main, then wraps canonical lifecycle resolution in a broad except Exception that silently ignores every non-CorrectionIntegrationError failure. It also accepts zero or multiple derived lifecycle tips by only checking tips[0] when tips is non-empty. Therefore an unavailable, malformed, ambiguous, or newer canonical remote lifecycle can be skipped and a stale integration candidate/ref can still be materialized from local assumptions, violating the exact current-main/cumulative-tip binding and fail-closed staleness requirements.
